However, reasoning is still brittle: small errors early on propagate forward to lead to confidently asserted but erroneous conclusions. This paper presents AutoCrit, a meta- reasoning system that incorporates structured self-criticism and iterative error-fixing directly into the CoT procedure. AutoCrit integrates a reasoning agent, a critique agent, and an execution monitor in an active feedback loop to detect and correct in- consistency proactively step by step. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K), commonsense inference (CSQA2), and interactive planning (ALFWorld) benchmarks, AutoCrit achieves accuracy improvements of 12–18% over baseline CoT and reduces error propagation rates by half. Theoretical analysis of AutoCrit as an iterative fixed-point system formally establishes it rigorously and provides error-propagation limits that demon- strate its scalability. This work advances LLM reliability by showing that incorporating critique into reasoning outperforms post-hoc validation, the foundation for future reasoning-intensive applications in AI-assisted decision-making.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202510.0587.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 10, 8]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6991012\", \"title\": [\"Automated Oversight Diagnostic Self-Correction and Failure-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents(ChinaMM)\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The rapid evolution of Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) has significantly advanced autonomous GUI agents. This paper presents AutoCrit, a meta- reasoning system that incorporates structured self-criticism and iterative error-fixing directly into the CoT procedure. AutoCrit integrates a reasoning agent, a critique agent, and an execution monitor in an active feedback loop to detect and correct in- consistency proactively step by step. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K), commonsense inference (CSQA2), and interactive planning (ALFWorld) benchmarks, AutoCrit achieves accuracy improvements of 12–18% over baseline CoT and reduces error propagation rates by half. This work advances LLM reliability by showing that incorporating critique into reasoning outperforms post-hoc validation, the foundation for future reasoning-intensive applications in AI-assisted decision-making.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202510.0587.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 10, 8]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6991012\", \"title\": [\"Automated Oversight Diagnostic Self-Correction and Failure-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents(ChinaMM)\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The rapid evolution of Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) has significantly advanced autonomous GUI agents. However, during the development of GUI agents for dynamic scenarios, error compounding leads to a labor-intensive and expensive bottleneck, requiring high costs for manual intervention. Meanwhile, errors are hard to be located and difficult to track failure reasoning. Consequently, it is challenging to overcome random errors simply by blindly increasing the size of the training dataset and address errors in a targeted manner. Existing research primarily attempt to improve GUI agent by optimizing the agent&apos;s internal design to avoid outcome deviation, ignoring the critical need for automated self-correction in step-level agent errors. In view of this, we propose the Automated Oversight (AO), an efficient four-stage closed-loop approach designed to emulate human-level oversight. The architecture consists of four key phases: (1) global outcome verification for final-state checking; (2) step-level visual trajectory alignment to intercept errors in real-time; (3) teacher-driven root-cause diagnosis to analyze failures; and (4) closed-loop rectification with state rollback to recover the task. Unlike traditional methods, AO focuses on failure-aware reasoning to identify the root causes of errors and execute targeted recovery. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can improve agent success rates and reduce human cognitive burden by achieving reliable autonomous interactions in dynamic systems.
